issues.description: The template's Main.java calls farm.feed(), but the problem specification and the solution implementation define and use feedAllAnimals() (and describe feedAllAnimals() in the task). Additionally, the template Farm.java does not provide a feedAllAnimals() method. This mismatch between the template Main usage and the expected method name/signature (as specified in the problem and implemented in the solution) can confuse students about which method to implement or invoke.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template consistent with the specification and solution by either (a) changing the commented call in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java from farm.feed() to farm.feedAllAnimals(), or (b) adding a feed() delegating method in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java that calls feedAllAnimals(). Also add a feedAllAnimals() stub in the template Farm.java (matching the signature described in the problem) so students have the correct method to implement.

issues.description: The sample Main in the template repository calls farm.feed(), while the problem statement and the solution implementation use the method name feedAllAnimals(). This is the same conceptual action (feeding all animals) but referenced with two different identifiers across artifacts, which can confuse students trying to map the example usage to the required API.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the call in the template Main from farm.feed() to farm.feedAllAnimals() (or vice versa update the problem statement and solution consistently). Prefer updating the template Main to use feedAllAnimals() to match the specified API in the problem statement and the solution.
